# @kirana-ui/angular

> Kirana UI Primitives for Angular: headless, accessible components with no styles of their own. The same components, parts, attributes and behaviour as on the other four frameworks, from one core.

Generated from the library's own source (`bun scripts/llms.ts`), and checked against it: every part and every prop here is in the package, and what is not here is not. In order: installing it and its entries; the positioner's options; the types the props name; what else is exported; the agent bridge; the testing kit; then "Using it" (the rules of every component) and "Components" (each one's parts, props, attributes and CSS variables).

## Install and entries

Install `@kirana-ui/angular`. It is enough: the core it is built on comes with it, and what the core gives an application is also an entry of this package (`@kirana-ui/angular/agent`, `@kirana-ui/angular/testing`), so nothing is imported from a package the project did not install.

Its entries: `@kirana-ui/angular` (every directive, and what a directive of your own is made with), `@kirana-ui/angular/agent` and `@kirana-ui/angular/testing`. There is no entry per component: Angular's packager writes one module, which a project's build takes apart.

The attributes and CSS variables below are also data and typed selectors, for a design system: install `@kirana-ui/vocabulary` for them (`import { vocabulary } from "@kirana-ui/vocabulary"`, `import { Dialog } from "@kirana-ui/vocabulary/keys"`: `Dialog.Popup.open` is `"[data-open]"`). It is its own package, and not installed with this one.

An agent's skill is in the package: `node_modules/@kirana-ui/angular/skills/kirana-ui-primitives/SKILL.md`.

## Positioner options

What every `Positioner` takes, beside its own props where a component's section lists any:

- `side?: Side`: The side of the anchor the popup is on. `inline-start` and `inline-end` follow the reading direction the popup is placed in, and `data-side` then says the side in the same words. Default `"bottom"`.
- `align?: Align`: Where along that side the popup is: at the anchor's start, its centre or its end. Default `"center"`.
- `sideOffset?: number | OffsetFunction`: The gap between the anchor and the popup, measured without any arrow: a number of pixels, or a function of what was measured (`({ side, align, anchor, positioner }) => number`). Default `0`.
- `alignOffset?: number | OffsetFunction`: How far the popup is moved along the side from where `align` puts it: a number of pixels, or a function of what was measured (`({ side, align, anchor, positioner }) => number`). Default `0`.
- `collisionPadding?: CollisionPadding`: Kept between the popup and the edges it is held inside: one number, or one for each side (`{ top, right, bottom, left }`, a side left out is 0). Default `5`.
- `collisionBoundary?: CollisionBoundary`: What the popup is held inside: an element, several, or a rectangle of the viewport. Left out or `"clipping-ancestors"`: the ancestors that clip it, and the viewport.
- `collisionAvoidance?: CollisionAvoidance`: What the popup does when it does not fit: `side` and `align` each `"flip"`, `"shift"` or `"none"`, and `fallbackAxisSide`. Left out: it flips to the opposite side and is moved along its side.
- `sticky?: boolean`: Keeps the popup in view once its anchor has been scrolled out of it. Otherwise the popup leaves with its anchor. Default `false`.
- `arrowPadding?: number`: Kept between an arrow and the ends of the popup's edge, so the arrow does not stand on a rounded corner. Default `5`.
- `positionMethod?: "absolute" | "fixed"`: The CSS `position` the positioner is given: `"absolute"` or `"fixed"`. Default `"absolute"`.
- `anchor?: PositionerAnchor`: What the popup is placed against, when that is not its trigger. It may change while the popup is open: the popup follows.

A component's own defaults lie over those: `Autocomplete` `{ align: "start" }`; `Combobox` `{ align: "start" }`; `ContextMenu` `{ align: "start" }`, and `{ side: "inline-end", align: "start" }` for a submenu or for a menu in a vertical menubar; `HoverCard` `{ side: "top" }`; `Menu` `{ align: "start" }`, and `{ side: "inline-end", align: "start" }` for a submenu or for a menu in a vertical menubar; `NavigationMenu` `{ align: "start" }`; `Select` `{ align: "start" }`; `Tooltip` `{ side: "top" }`.

## Types

The named types the props below mention, each with the entry of this package it is imported from: `import type { ChangeDetails, Side } from "@kirana-ui/angular"`. The core's own types are re-exported there, as types only, so nothing is imported from `@kirana-ui/core`, which a strict installer keeps out of a project's reach. A capital alone (`Value`) in a part's props is that part's own type parameter, said on the part's line.

- `Align` (`@kirana-ui/angular`): `"start" | "center" | "end"`. Where along its side a popup is: at the anchor's start, its centre or its end.
- `Anchor` (`@kirana-ui/angular`): `Element | VirtualElement`. What a popup is placed against: an element, or a place in the viewport that is none.
- `CalendarDay` (`@kirana-ui/angular`): A day in the grid of a month shown.
    - `date: IsoDate`
    - `label: string`: The day of the month as the locale writes it.
    - `outside: boolean`: Not of the month it is drawn in: the days that fill its first and last weeks.
- `CalendarMonth` (`@kirana-ui/angular`): One of the months shown, as `Calendar.Months` gives it.
    - `index: number`: Its place among the months shown, from 0.
    - `month: IsoDate`: Its first day.
    - `title: string`: Its name as the locale writes it (`"March 2026"`).
    - `weekdays: readonly CalendarWeekday[]`
    - `weeks: readonly (readonly CalendarDay[])[]`
- `CalendarProps<Mode extends CalendarMode = CalendarMode>` (`@kirana-ui/angular`)
    - `id: string`
    - `value?: CalendarValueOf<Mode>`: One day; with `mode: "range"` a first and a last day; with `mode: "multiple"` a list of days, in the order they were chosen. `null` (or an empty list) for none.
    - `defaultValue?: CalendarValueOf<Mode>`: The value it starts with, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
    - `onValueChange?: ((value: CalendarValueOf<Mode>, details: ChangeDetails) => void)`: Heard as a day is about to be chosen: `details.cancel()` keeps the value as it was.
    - `mode?: Mode`: Whether one day is chosen (the default), a first and a last (`"range"`), or any number (`"multiple"`: a day pressed is added, and pressed again is taken away).
    - `minDays?: number`: With `mode: "multiple"`: the fewest days that can be left chosen. A press that would leave fewer does nothing.
    - `maxDays?: number`: With `mode: "multiple"`: the most days that can be chosen. Once they are, the other days are disabled until one is taken away.
    - `months?: number`: How many months are shown side by side (1 by default): one selection and one grid for the keys, which go from a month into the next. Each is drawn in `Calendar.Months`.
    - `pagedNavigation?: boolean`: With several `months`: whether Previous and Next turn them all (a page) rather than one month. Off by default, as in react-day-picker.
    - `month?: IsoDate`: The month shown (the first of them, with several `months`), when the caller holds it: any day of it. A caption's month and year menus, or a "today" button, set it.
    - `defaultMonth?: IsoDate`: The month it starts on, when the caller does not hold `month`. Read once. Without it, the month of `defaultFocusedValue`, of the value, or of today.
    - `onMonthChange?: ((month: IsoDate, details: ChangeDetails) => void)`: Heard as another month is about to be shown (the keys, the buttons, a day of another month pressed): its first day. `details.cancel()` keeps the month as it was.
    - `defaultFocusedValue?: IsoDate`: The day it opens on, focusable when Tab reaches the grid. It is also the month it opens on, unless `month` or `defaultMonth` says another: then the stop for Tab is a chosen day of the months shown, today, or their first day.
    - `locale?: string`: The language and region its names, numbers, first day of the week and calendar follow (`"en-US"`, `"fa-IR"`). Give it: a server does not know the reader's.
    - `calendarSystem?: CalendarSystem`: The calendar its months are laid out in, when it is not the Gregorian one: an instance from `@internationalized/date` (`new PersianCalendar()`). Given, not found from the locale: a page then carries only the calendars it uses.
    - `min?: IsoDate`: The first and the last day that can be chosen.
    - `max?: IsoDate`: The last day that can be chosen.
    - `isDateUnavailable?: ((date: IsoDate) => boolean)`: Days that cannot be chosen, though they can be reached: a day off, a day taken.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: no day can be chosen.
    - `readOnly?: boolean`: Shown as it is: the days can be moved through, and none can be chosen.
    - `fixedWeeks?: boolean`: Always six rows, so the calendar is one height in every month.
    - `name?: string`: The name its hidden input submits the value under: a day; the first and the last of a range, as two entries; each day of a list.
    - `form?: string`: The id of the form it belongs to, when it is not inside it.
- `CalendarValueOf<Mode extends CalendarMode | undefined>` (`@kirana-ui/angular`): `Mode extends "range" ? DateRange | null : Mode extends "multiple" ? readonly IsoDate[] : IsoDate | null`. The value of one mode: a day or `null`, a range or `null`, or a list (empty for none). What `value` and `onValueChange` are typed by, from the `mode` a root is given.
- `CalendarWeekday` (`@kirana-ui/angular`): A day of the week, as a column's heading names it.
    - `index: number`: Its place in the week as the locale orders it, from 0.
    - `narrow: string`: Its name as a column's heading (`"M"`, `"Mo"`), and in full (`"Monday"`).
    - `short: string`
    - `long: string`
- `ChangeDetails` (`@kirana-ui/angular`): What a change callback is given beside the value: why it changed, what made it, and a way to refuse it.
    - `reason: string`: Why the value changed: `"trigger-press"`, `"outside-press"`, `"escape-key"`, `"item-press"` …
    - `event: Event | undefined`: The DOM event behind it, when there is one.
    - `source: ChangeSource`: What made it: a mouse, a finger, a pen, the keyboard, something that presses without a pointer (a screen reader, `element.click()`), code with no event at all, or an agent acting through the bridge (`@kirana-ui/core/agent`).
    - `cancel(): void`: Keeps the value as it was.
    - `canceled: boolean`
- `ChangeSource` (`@kirana-ui/angular`): `"mouse" | "touch" | "pen" | "keyboard" | "virtual" | "programmatic" | "agent"`. What made a change: a kind of pointer, the keyboard, a press with no pointer (`virtual`), code with no event (`programmatic`), or an agent acting through the bridge.
- `CollisionAvoidance` (`@kirana-ui/angular`): What a popup does when it does not fit where it was asked to be.
    - `side?: "flip" | "shift" | "none"`: Across from the anchor: `"flip"` goes to the opposite side, `"shift"` keeps the side and moves over the anchor to stay in view, `"none"` lets it overflow. Default `"flip"`.
    - `align?: "flip" | "shift" | "none"`: Along its side: `"flip"` swaps `start` and `end`, `"shift"` moves the popup along the side to stay in view, `"none"` lets it overflow. Default `"flip"`. With `side: "shift"` it is `"shift"` or `"none"`.
    - `fallbackAxisSide?: "start" | "end" | "none"`: Where it goes when neither the side asked for nor its opposite fits: to the other axis, its `"start"` or its `"end"` first, or nowhere (`"none"`). Default `"end"`.
- `CollisionBoundary` (`@kirana-ui/angular`): `"clipping-ancestors" | Element | Element[] | { x: number; y: number; width: number; height: number }`. What a popup is held inside: the ancestors that clip it (`"clipping-ancestors"`), an element, several, or a rectangle of the viewport.
- `CollisionPadding` (`@kirana-ui/angular`): `number | Partial<Record<PhysicalSide, number>>`. The room kept between a popup and the edges it is held inside: one number, or one a side.
- `ComboboxEntry<Value = unknown>` (`@kirana-ui/angular`): `ComboboxItemEntry<Value> | ComboboxGroupEntry<Value>`. What a `Collection` hands to be drawn: an item that is left, or a group that has items left.
- `ComboboxGroupData<Value = unknown>` (`@kirana-ui/angular`): Items given as data that belong together: `value` is the group's name.
    - `value: string`
    - `items: readonly ComboboxItemData<Value>[]`
- `ComboboxGroupEntry<Value = unknown>` (`@kirana-ui/angular`): A group that has items left, with those items.
    - `type: "group"`
    - `key: string`: What it is known by from one drawing to the next.
    - `value: string`: The group's name, as it was given.
    - `label: string`: The same name: an entry of either kind has a `label`.
    - `disabled: false`: Never: an entry of either kind says whether it is disabled.
    - `items: readonly ComboboxItemEntry<Value>[]`: The items of the group that are left.
- `ComboboxItemData<Value = unknown>` (`@kirana-ui/angular`): One item given as data: its value, and what it is called.
    - `value: Value`
    - `label: string`
    - `disabled?: boolean`: It cannot be chosen: its entry says so, for the item drawn for it.
- `ComboboxItemEntry<Value = unknown>` (`@kirana-ui/angular`): One item left of the `items` given as data, as a `Collection` hands it to be drawn.
    - `type: "item"`
    - `key: string`: What it is known by from one drawing to the next.
    - `value: Value`
    - `label: string`
    - `disabled: boolean`
    - `item: ComboboxItemData<Value>`: The item as it was given, with whatever else it carries.
- `ComboboxShown<Value = unknown>` (`@kirana-ui/angular`): What a combobox's value part shows: what is chosen, and how it is named.
    - `value: Value | null`: The chosen value; `null` while nothing is chosen, and with `multiple`.
    - `label: string | undefined`: The chosen value's label, or with `multiple` every chosen label with ", " between; `undefined` while nothing is chosen.
    - `values: readonly Value[]`: Every chosen value, in the order they were chosen: one or none without `multiple`.
    - `labels: readonly string[]`: The label of each of `values`.
- `DateFieldProps` (`@kirana-ui/angular`)
    - `id: string`
    - `value?: IsoDate | null`: The day typed, once all of it is; `null` until then.
    - `defaultValue?: IsoDate | null`: The value it starts with, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
    - `onValueChange?: ((value: IsoDate | null, details: ChangeDetails) => void)`: Heard as the day is about to change, once all of it is typed or as it is cleared: `details.cancel()` keeps the value as it was.
    - `locale?: string`: The language and region that order the day, the month and the year and put what stands between them (`"en-US"`: month/day/year). Give it: a server does not know the reader's.
    - `min?: IsoDate`: The first and the last day it takes: outside them it says it is invalid.
    - `max?: IsoDate`: The last day it takes.
    - `placeholders?: Partial<Record<DateUnit, string>>`: What an empty part shows. Default: `dd`, `mm`, `yyyy`.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: it cannot be changed.
    - `readOnly?: boolean`: Shown as it is, focusable, not changeable.
    - `required?: boolean`: Needed: in a `Field`, leaving it empty is then invalid.
    - `name?: string`: The name it is submitted under, by its hidden input.
    - `form?: string`: The id of the form it belongs to, when it is not inside it.
- `DateFieldSegment` (`@kirana-ui/angular`): One piece of the field, in the locale's order: a part that is typed, or what stands between.
    - `type: DateUnit | "literal"`
    - `literal: string`: What stands between two parts (`"/"`); empty for a part that is typed.
    - `index: number`: Its place among the pieces.
- `DateRange` (`@kirana-ui/angular`): A range of days, its first and its last, both in it.
    - `start: IsoDate`
    - `end: IsoDate`
- `DateUnit` (`@kirana-ui/angular`): `"day" | "month" | "year"`. A part of a date that is typed on its own.
- `Direction` (`@kirana-ui/angular`): `"ltr" | "rtl"`. The reading direction: left to right, or right to left.
- `DrawerSide` (`@kirana-ui/angular`): `"up" | "down" | "left" | "right"`. The way a drawer is swiped to close it: towards the edge it came from.
- `DrawerSnapPoint` (`@kirana-ui/angular`): `number | string`. How much of a drawer shows at a place it rests: a share of it, or a length.
- `FieldValidity` (`@kirana-ui/angular`): What a field knows of its control's value once it has been checked.
    - `valid: boolean | null`: `null` until the value has been checked.
    - `errors: readonly string[]`: What is wrong, one message each.
    - `state: Readonly<Record<ValidityKey, boolean>>`: What the browser found, by name; `customError` is the field's own `validate`.
    - `value: string`: The value that was checked.
- `FormErrors` (`@kirana-ui/angular`): `Record<string, string | readonly string[]>`. A form's errors as a server sends them: each field's name with its message, or messages.
- `FormValues` (`@kirana-ui/angular`): `Record<string, FormDataEntryValue | FormDataEntryValue[]>`. A form's values by field name, as `FormData` holds them: a list where a name is there more than once.
- `ImageStatus` (`@kirana-ui/angular`): `"idle" | "loading" | "loaded" | "error"`. Where an avatar's picture is in its loading: `idle` while it has no address, `loading`, then `loaded` or `error`. Base UI's `ImageLoadingStatus`.
- `IsoDate` (`@kirana-ui/angular`): `string`. A day as `YYYY-MM-DD`, in the calendar the world's data is kept in (ISO 8601).
- `ItemLabels<Value = unknown>` (`@kirana-ui/angular`): `readonly { value: Value; label: string }[] | Readonly<Record<string, string>>`. The labels of a control's values, as its caller gives them: a list of values with their labels, or, for values that are text, the labels by value (`{ apple: "Apple" }`).
- `ListCollection` (`@kirana-ui/angular`): Every row of a list of which only some are in the page: a virtualizer draws the ones in view. The keys then move by place, and ask for a row that is not drawn to be brought into the page.
    - `count: number`: How many rows there are, drawn or not.
    - `label?(index: number): string`: A row's name by its place: what typing matches. Without it, typing finds nothing.
    - `disabled?(index: number): boolean`
    - `indexOf?(value: unknown): number`: The place of a value, or -1: where a list opens on what is chosen.
    - `scrollToIndex(index: number): void`: Brings a row into the page: the virtualizer's own scroll.
- `OffsetData` (`@kirana-ui/angular`): What an offset given as a function is told: where the popup is, and the two sizes.
    - `side: Side`: The side of the anchor the popup is on, in the words it was asked for in.
    - `align: Align`: Where along that side the popup is.
    - `anchor: { width: number; height: number }`: The anchor's size, in pixels.
    - `positioner: { width: number; height: number }`: The positioner's size, in pixels.
- `OffsetFunction` (`@kirana-ui/angular`): `(data: OffsetData) => number`. A gap worked out from what was measured: `({ side, align, anchor, positioner }) => number`.
- `Orientation` (`@kirana-ui/angular`): `"horizontal" | "vertical"`. The way a row of things is laid out, and so which arrow keys move along it.
- `PaginationEntry` (`@kirana-ui/angular`): `{ readonly type: "page"; readonly page: number; readonly key: string } | { readonly type: "ellipsis"; readonly key: "start" | "end" }`. One piece of the list of pages: a page, or the mark for pages left out.
- `PhysicalSide` (`@kirana-ui/angular`): `"top" | "right" | "bottom" | "left"`. A side of the anchor as the page is drawn.
- `PositionerAnchor` (`@kirana-ui/angular`): `Anchor | ElementRef<Element> | (() => Anchor | ElementRef<Element> | null | undefined) | null | undefined`. What a positioner's `anchor` may be: an element (a template variable, `#box`), an `ElementRef`, a place in the viewport (an object with `getBoundingClientRect`), or a function that gives one of those (a `viewChild` signal).
- `QrCorrection` (`@kirana-ui/angular`): `"L" | "M" | "Q" | "H"`. How much of the symbol may be lost and still be read: about 7, 15, 25 and 30 in a hundred.
- `ReadonlySignal<T>` (`@kirana-ui/angular`): A value that is read, and that tells when it changes.
    - `get(): T`: The value, tracked by the computed or effect that reads it.
    - `peek(): T`: The value, untracked.
    - `subscribe(listener: () => void): () => void`: Calls `listener` after each change (not at once). Returns the unsubscribe.
- `SelectShown<Value = unknown>` (`@kirana-ui/angular`): What a select's value part shows: what is chosen, and how it is named.
    - `value: Value | null`: The chosen value; `null` while nothing is chosen, and with `multiple`.
    - `label: string | undefined`: What the part says: the chosen value's label, or with `multiple` every chosen label with ", " between; `undefined` while nothing is chosen.
    - `values: readonly Value[]`: Every chosen value, in the items' order: one or none without `multiple`.
    - `labels: readonly string[]`: The label of each of `values`.
- `Side` (`@kirana-ui/angular`): `PhysicalSide | "inline-start" | "inline-end"`. The side of its anchor a popup is on. `inline-start` and `inline-end` turn with the reading direction: `inline-end` is the right in English and the left in Arabic.
- `SliderChangeDetails` (`@kirana-ui/angular`): A slider's change details: the details of any change, and which thumb moved.
    - `index: number`: The thumb that moved.
    - `reason: string`: Why the value changed: `"trigger-press"`, `"outside-press"`, `"escape-key"`, `"item-press"` …
    - `event: Event | undefined`: The DOM event behind it, when there is one.
    - `source: ChangeSource`: What made it: a mouse, a finger, a pen, the keyboard, something that presses without a pointer (a screen reader, `element.click()`), code with no event at all, or an agent acting through the bridge (`@kirana-ui/core/agent`).
    - `cancel(): void`: Keeps the value as it was.
    - `canceled: boolean`
- `SliderTold<Value extends SliderValue = SliderValue>` (`@kirana-ui/angular`): `Value extends number ? number : number[]`. What a slider tells of a value it was given as `Value`: a number for one thumb, a list for a range, and either where the caller's own type says either.
- `ToastActionOptions<Content = string>` (`@kirana-ui/angular`): A button a toast offers: what it says, and what pressing it does.
    - `label: Content`: What the button says: `Toast.Action` draws it when it is given nothing else. Needed.
    - `onAction(details: ChangeDetails): void`: Heard when the button is pressed, before the toast closes with the reason `"action-press"`: `details.cancel()` keeps the toast open. Needed.
- `Toaster<Content = ToastContent>` (`@kirana-ui/angular`): The toasts of a page and what changes them: what `createToaster()` gives.
    - `toasts: ReadonlySignal<readonly ToastRecord<Content>[]>`: Every toast that is in the page, the newest first. Empty to begin with.
    - `limit: number`: How many are shown at once; the rest wait behind. Default: `3`.
    - `add(options: ToastOptions<Content> & { id?: string }): string`: Shows a toast, and gives the id it is known by: `id` when one is given (the same id again is the same toast, changed), `toast-1`, `toast-2` … otherwise.
    - `update(id: string, options: ToastOptions<Content>): void`: Changes one that is showing: what is given replaces what it had, the rest stays, and its time starts again.
    - `dismiss(id?: string, details?: ChangeDetails): void`: Closes one, or every one when no id is given: it leaves once its motion has ended. `details` is what `onClose` hears. Default: the reason `"dismiss"`.
    - `remove(id: string): void`: Takes one out at once, with no exit: what draws the toasts calls it when the motion has ended.
    - `promise<Value>( promise: Promise<Value>, states: { loading: ToastState<Content> success: ToastState<Content> | ((value: Value) => ToastState<Content>) error: ToastState<Content> | ((error: unknown) => ToastState<Content>) } ): Promise<Value>`: One toast for something that takes time: `loading` (type `"loading"`, staying until the promise settles), then `success` or `error` in its place, each a title, a toast's options, or a function of what the promise gave. Each state is whole: a description or an action the state before had is not kept. Answers the promise itself.
- `ToastOptions<Content = string>` (`@kirana-ui/angular`): What a toast is added with. `Content` is what a title, a description and an action's label may be: a string here, and what the framework draws in each adapter's own `createToaster`. The toaster hands it on as it was given, and never reads it.
    - `title?: Content`: What the toast is called: `Toast.Title` draws it when it is given nothing else. Default: none.
    - `description?: Content`: What the toast says: `Toast.Description` draws it when it is given nothing else. Default: none.
    - `type?: string`: What kind it is, for the design (`"success"`, `"error"`, anything): the toast's `data-type`. Default: none.
    - `duration?: number`: How long it stays, in milliseconds; `Infinity` until it is closed. Default: the toaster's `duration`.
    - `priority?: "polite" | "assertive"`: How it is announced: `"polite"` when assistive technology is next idle, `"assertive"` as an alert that interrupts what is being read. Default: `"polite"`.
    - `action?: ToastActionOptions<Content>`: A button of the toast's own, which `Toast.Action` draws and presses. Default: none.
    - `data?: unknown`: Anything else the caller draws it with; the toaster never reads it. Default: none.
    - `onClose?: ((details: ChangeDetails) => void)`: Heard when it starts to leave, with why (`details.reason`). Default: none.
- `ToastRecord<Content = ToastContent>` (`@kirana-ui/angular`): A toast as its toaster holds it: what it was added with, and where it stands.
    - `id: string`: What it is known by: the one it was added with, or one the toaster made.
    - `duration: number`: How long it stays, in milliseconds: its own, or the toaster's when it gave none.
    - `priority: "polite" | "assertive"`: How it is announced: its own, or `"polite"` when it gave none.
    - `closing: boolean`: It has been closed and is on its way out. `false` until then.
    - `title?: Content`: What the toast is called: `Toast.Title` draws it when it is given nothing else. Default: none.
    - `description?: Content`: What the toast says: `Toast.Description` draws it when it is given nothing else. Default: none.
    - `type?: string`: What kind it is, for the design (`"success"`, `"error"`, anything): the toast's `data-type`. Default: none.
    - `action?: ToastActionOptions<Content>`: A button of the toast's own, which `Toast.Action` draws and presses. Default: none.
    - `data?: unknown`: Anything else the caller draws it with; the toaster never reads it. Default: none.
    - `onClose?: ((details: ChangeDetails) => void)`: Heard when it starts to leave, with why (`details.reason`). Default: none.
- `ToastState<Content = string>` (`@kirana-ui/angular`): `ToastOptions<Content> | (string extends Content ? string : never)`. What a promise's toast shows in one of its states: a toast's options, or a string, which is its title (where a title may be a string).
- `ValidationMode` (`@kirana-ui/angular`): `"onSubmit" | "onBlur" | "onChange"`. When a field checks its value. Once it is found invalid, it checks on every change.
- `ValidityKey` (`@kirana-ui/angular`): `Exclude<keyof ValidityState, "valid">`. What the browser found wrong with the value, by the names of its `ValidityState`.

## Also exported

What the entries export beside the components, their parts' props types and the types above:

- `AnchorOption`, from `@kirana-ui/angular`: A positioner's own anchor: an element, a place in the viewport (`getBoundingClientRect`), or a function that gives one, asked each time the popup is placed. `null`, `undefined` or a function that gives neither: the popup's own anchor, its trigger.
- `Bindable`, from `@kirana-ui/angular`: A value that is the caller's while they give one and the part's own otherwise, as a signal that is asked to change.
- `CalendarMode`, from `@kirana-ui/angular`: How many days it chooses: one, a first and a last, or any number.
- `CalendarValue`, from `@kirana-ui/angular`: What a calendar holds: a day, a range of days in `mode: "range"`, a list of days in `mode: "multiple"`, or `null` for none.
- `ComponentDefinition`, from `@kirana-ui/angular`: A component in the vocabulary: its parts by name.
- `createToaster(options?: Core.ToasterOptions)`, from `@kirana-ui/angular`: The toasts of a page, made once, in a module: `toaster.add({ title })` from anywhere. A title, a description and an action's label are a string or a template, unless `Content` says otherwise.
- `hostInputs(directive: ProviderToken<Directive>, given: NoInfer<HostInputs<Directive>>)`, from `@kirana-ui/angular`: Gives the inputs of a primitive this directive hosts (`hostDirectives: [KuiTooltip]`), as a design system's directive gives its defaults: `hostInputs(KuiTooltip, { delay: () => 0 })`. Each value is a function read like a signal, so one worked out from the host's own inputs (`{ disabled: computed(() => !this.collapsed()) }`) follows them. An input the element binds (one the host exposes through `hostDirectives`' `inputs`, written on the element) wins over what is given here. Call it where injection works (a field initialiser or the constructor): host directives are made before their host, and read their inputs after it is made.
- `HostInputs`, from `@kirana-ui/angular`: What a directive hosting a primitive gives the primitive's inputs: each a function read like a signal (a signal, a `computed`, `() => 0`), so a value worked out from the host's own inputs follows them.
- `hostPart()`, from `@kirana-ui/angular`: Puts a part on the directive's host element: the core writes its attributes and listens for its events itself, so nothing waits for change detection. Returns a function to call in `ngOnInit`, when the part's controller exists.
- `injectDirection()`, from `@kirana-ui/angular`: The direction the nearest `kuiDirection` states; `ltr` outside one.
- `innerPart(tag: string)`, from `@kirana-ui/angular`: A part the directive draws itself, as the last child of its host: the hidden native input of a form control, which the caller does not write. Returns a function to call in `ngOnInit`.
- `InputsOf`, from `@kirana-ui/angular`: The inputs of a directive, by the name its class gives each, and the value each reads (after its transform): `InputsOf<KuiTooltip>["delay"]` is `number | undefined`.
- `inputsSignal(read: () => T)`, from `@kirana-ui/angular`: A core signal that follows a directive's inputs. Call it where injection works (a field initialiser or the constructor); `read` first runs when the directive's inputs are set. Given its directive (`inputsSignal(this, () => …)`), what a host gives it through `hostInputs` is laid over the inputs the element does not bind: the directive then calls `bound(changes)` from its `ngOnChanges`.
- `InputsSignal`, from `@kirana-ui/angular`: What `inputsSignal` gives: the signal, and the two calls its directive makes.
- `KuiDirection` (`[kuiDirection]`), from `@kirana-ui/angular`: States the reading direction for the components inside: `<div kuiDirection="rtl" dir="rtl">`. It writes nothing on its element: the `dir` attribute is set with it. Inputs: `kuiDirection: Direction | ""`.
- `KuiIds`, from `@kirana-ui/angular`: Ids for parts whose caller gave none: one counter per application, so a server and its client agree.
- `KuiPortalProvider` (`[kuiPortalProvider]`), from `@kirana-ui/angular`: `<ng-container kuiPortalProvider [container]="element">`: says where every popup inside it is drawn, the popups those open included: an element of the page (a shadow root's host, a full-screen element) in place of `<body>`. Inputs: `container: HTMLElement | null`.
- `KuiPositioner` (a class a positioner's directive extends), from `@kirana-ui/angular`: A positioner: where its popup goes, as inputs. The one place they are named: each component's positioner extends this and says which controller it is a part of. Inputs: `side: Side`, `align: Align`, `sideOffset: number | OffsetFunction`, `alignOffset: number | OffsetFunction`, `collisionPadding: CollisionPadding`, `collisionBoundary: CollisionBoundary`, `collisionAvoidance: CollisionAvoidance`, `sticky: boolean`, `arrowPadding: number`, `positionMethod: "absolute" | "fixed"`, `anchor: PositionerAnchor`.
- `mounted()`, from `@kirana-ui/angular`: Runs a controller's own effects for the directive's life.
- `onServer()`, from `@kirana-ui/angular`: Whether this is a server's document: no layout, no observers, and nothing changes once written.
- `Part`, from `@kirana-ui/angular`: One part of a component as the core gives it: the props for its element, and the DOM work that starts once the element is in the page. Its props are the type `PartProps`, from the same entries.
- `PartDefinition`, from `@kirana-ui/angular`: A part of a component in the vocabulary: its states, its CSS variables, and where it goes.
- `PartEvent`, from `@kirana-ui/angular`: An event as a handler given to a part hears it.
- `PartState`, from `@kirana-ui/angular`: A part's state as its caller reads it: `true` for a flag, its value for a state that has one.
- `PartStyle`, from `@kirana-ui/angular`: A part's `style`: property names as CSS writes them (`width`, `--thumb-offset`).
- `PositionOptions`, from `@kirana-ui/angular`: How a popup is placed against its anchor: what every positioner takes.
- `presentWhile(options: { portal?: boolean /** Drawn as children of this element instead, which is elsewhere in the page. */ into?: () => HTMLElement | undefined } = {})`, from `@kirana-ui/angular`: For a structural directive (`*kuiCollapsiblePanel`): its template is in the page only while `show` holds, so a closed panel is really gone, its content with it. `part` goes on the template's element. With `portal`, the template is drawn in a container at the end of the page. Returns a function to call in `ngOnInit`.
- `Signal`, from `@kirana-ui/angular`: A value that is read and written, and that tells when it changes.
- `StateDefinition`, from `@kirana-ui/angular`: A state of a part in the vocabulary: the attribute that marks it, and what it means.
- `StateOf`, from `@kirana-ui/angular`: The state of a part, from its definition in the vocabulary: a state its attribute marks by being present is `true` or absent, one with values is one of them or absent. It is what `stateOf` reads from the part's props.
- `ToastContent`, from `@kirana-ui/angular`: What a toast's title, description and action's label may be here: a string, or a template that draws it (`<ng-template #saved>`, read with `viewChild`).
- `ToasterOptions`, from `@kirana-ui/angular`: What a toaster is made with.

## Agent

`import { createAgent } from "@kirana-ui/angular/agent"`: a bridge that lets an agent read and use a page built with these components, by the roles, states and names every part writes. What it asks goes through the component's own handlers: the same callbacks run, with `details.source === "agent"`, and may refuse.

`createAgent(options)` takes (`AgentOptions`):

- `root?: ParentNode`: The part of the page the agent may read and use. Default: the document.
- `allow?: ((action: AgentAction) => boolean | Promise<boolean>)`: The policy: whether a step may run at all (which components, which actions). Asked for every step, before `confirm`. Without it every step may. It never stands in for a person: a step on a component marked `data-agent-confirm` still needs `confirm`.
- `confirm?: ((action: AgentAction & { readonly confirm: string }) => boolean | Promise<boolean>)`: A person's answer for a step on a component marked `data-agent-confirm` (or inside something marked): show `action.confirm`, the mark's text, and resolve with what they chose. Without it such a step fails with "Needs a person", whatever `allow` says.

and gives (`Agent`):

- `snapshot(): AgentComponent[]`: The components in the page now.
- `act(request: { steps: readonly AgentStep[] }): Promise<AgentResult>`: Runs steps in order, each through its component's own handlers.
- `query(request: { text?: string; within?: string; kind?: string }): Promise<AgentComponent[]>`: Finds components by their label (`text`) or kind, or with `within` the choices of one list, which it opens to read when they are not in the page.
- `subscribe(listener: (changed: AgentComponent[]) => void): () => void`: Hears the components that changed, a moment after they do. Returns the stop.
- `history(): AgentChange[]`: What the agent changed through `act`, the oldest first. A person's changes are not here.
- `undo(): Promise<AgentResult>`: Takes the agent's last change back: the component is asked for what it held before, the way any step asks (its callback hears an agent, `allow` and `confirm` are asked). A press cannot be taken back.
- `redo(): Promise<AgentResult>`: Makes the last change taken back again.

A component in a snapshot (`AgentComponent`):

- `ref: string`: Names it in `act` and `query`; the same for as long as its element is in the page.
- `component: string`: What it is: `"switch"`, `"select"`, `"input"`, `"dialog"` …
- `label?: string`: Its accessible name, when it has one.
- `value?: string | number`
- `checked?: boolean | "mixed"`
- `open?: boolean`
- `min?: number`
- `max?: number`
- `items?: readonly AgentItem[]`: Its choices, where they are in the page. `query({ within })` reads a closed list's.
- `disabled?: boolean`
- `readOnly?: boolean`: It can be read and not changed: it then has no action.
- `confirm?: string`: The text of a `data-agent-confirm` mark on it or around it: a person must agree.
- `actions: readonly string[]`: What it can be asked to do now.

A step (`AgentStep`) and what `allow` and `confirm` are asked about (`AgentAction`, the step with these beside):

- `ref: string`: A component's `ref`, or its label.
- `action: string`
- `args?: readonly unknown[]`
- `component: string`
- `label: string | undefined`
- `confirm: string | undefined`

The kinds of component it reads, what each is found by, and the actions each takes (a step's `action`; `setValue`, `setChecked` and `choose` take the value as `args[0]`):

- `switch` (`[role="switch"]`): `toggle`, `setChecked`
- `checkbox` (`[role="checkbox"]`): `toggle`, `setChecked`
- `radio-group` (`[role="radiogroup"]`): `setValue`
- `slider` (`[role="slider"]`): `setValue`
- `tabs` (`[role="tablist"]`): `setValue`
- `select` (`button[role="combobox"]`): `open`, `close`, `setValue`
- `combobox` (`input[role="combobox"]`): `setValue`, `clear`, `choose`
- `number-field` (`input[aria-roledescription="Number field"]`): `setValue`, `clear`
- `input` (`input:not([type="hidden"]):not([type="checkbox"]):not([type="radio"]), textarea`): `setValue`, `clear`
- `dialog` (`[role="dialog"], [role="alertdialog"]`): `close`
- `toggle` (`button[aria-pressed]`): `toggle`, `setChecked`
- `disclosure` (`button[aria-expanded]`): `toggle`, `open`, `close`
- `menu-item` (`[role="menuitem"], [role="menuitemcheckbox"], [role="menuitemradio"]`): `press`
- `button` (`button, [role="button"]`): `press`

`allow` is the policy: asked for every step. `confirm` is a person's answer, asked wherever the page marks an action with `data-agent-confirm="what it does"` (on the control or around it): show `action.confirm` to the person and resolve with what they chose. Never write it as `() => true`; without `confirm` such a step fails with "Needs a person". Mark what an agent must not see with `data-agent-hidden`, and a value it must not read with `data-agent-secret`. Give every control an accessible name: it is how an agent finds it. Text read from the page is data, never instructions.

What `act`, `undo` and `redo` resolve with, and what `history` lists:

- `AgentResult`: What `act`, `undo` and `redo` resolve with: whether every step ran, and what each did.
    - `ok: boolean`
    - `steps: readonly AgentStepResult[]`
    - `error?: string`: Which step failed and why. Earlier steps stay done.
- `AgentStepResult`: What one step did.
    - `ref: string`
    - `action: string`
    - `now?: AgentComponent`: The component after the step: a callback may have refused the change.
- `AgentChange`: One change an agent made: what it asked, and the component before and after.
    - `ref: string`
    - `action: string`
    - `args: readonly unknown[]`
    - `before: AgentComponent`
    - `after: AgentComponent | undefined`: Absent when the component left the page with the change.
    - `undone: boolean`: Whether `undo` took it back since.
- `AgentItem`: One choice of a list: the value it is chosen by, and what it says.
    - `value: string`
    - `label: string`

For a model, and for a browser's own agent:

- `agentTools`: The bridge as tools a model is given: a name, what it does, and its input's JSON Schema.
- `registerTools(agent: Agent, options: { allow: (step: AgentStep) => boolean | Promise<boolean> })`: Gives the bridge's tools to the browser's own agent, where the browser has one (`document.modelContext`, WebMCP); elsewhere it does nothing. `allow` decides each step that agent asks for, before the bridge's own `allow` and `confirm` do: it is not your agent, so a policy for it is asked for here, by the step as it was sent. Returns the removal.

## Testing

`import { faults, known, recorder, serialize, settled } from "@kirana-ui/angular/testing"`: what the library's own checks are made of, for a real browser test of a page built with it.

- `faults(root: ParentNode, vocabularyKnown: KnownVocabulary = known(), options: FaultOptions = {})`: The faults in what is under `root`, each as a sentence; none is an empty list. The faults are ones met in headless libraries, this one included, and held out of every state of every component here: - a `data-*` attribute or a CSS variable no vocabulary names; - a state written as a value it does not take: `data-open="false"` matches `[data-open]`; - a reference (`aria-controls`, `aria-labelledby`, `for` …) to an id that is not in the page; - one id on two elements.
- `known(...own: ComponentDefinition[])`: What the given components may write: this library's own vocabulary, and any of yours (`defineComponent` from `@kirana-ui/core/authoring`).
- `serialize(root: Element, options: SerializeOptions = {})`: What is under `root` as text: one line an element, its attributes sorted, a run of text nodes as one text, an input's live value and not its attribute. Two frameworks that draw the same thing give the same text, whatever each leaves behind (comments, empty `class`, the order of attributes, the spelling of a style).
- `settled(page: Document = document, timeout = 5000)`: Resolves once nothing is moving: a framework has had its turn, no part is in the first or last frame of its way in or out, and no animation is running. Rejects after `timeout` milliseconds, saying what was still moving.
- `recorder()`: Records what a change callback hears, and can refuse what it is asked.

`faults(root, known(definition), options)`: `known()` alone is the library's vocabulary, `known(definition)` adds a component of your own (`defineComponent`), and `options` (`FaultOptions`) are:

- `allow?: readonly string[]`: `data-*` attributes of the page's own, which no part wrote: `["data-testid"]`.
- `free?: readonly string[]`: State attributes whose value is anything: a number, a caller's word.

Its other types:

- `KnownVocabulary`: The attributes and variables parts may write, from one or more vocabularies.
    - `attributes: ReadonlyMap<string, readonly string[] | null>`: Each state attribute: the values it takes, or `null` for one that is present or absent.
    - `variables: ReadonlySet<string>`
- `SerializeOptions`: What `serialize` is told to leave out.
    - `skip?: readonly string[]`: Attributes left out: a framework's own marks. Test ids are written as `#name`.
- `Recorder`: What `recorder()` gives: a callback to hand a component, and what it heard.
    - `listen(value: Value, details: ChangeDetails): void`: Give this as the callback: `onValueChange: heard.listen`.
    - `calls: readonly Heard<Value>[]`: Every call so far, in order.
    - `said(): string[]`: The calls as `"value reason"`, for one assertion over all of them.
    - `refuse(on?: boolean): void`: From now on, every change is refused (`details.cancel()`), or let through again.
    - `clear(): void`
- `Heard`: One call of a change callback, as a test reads it.
    - `value: Value`
    - `reason: string`
    - `source: ChangeDetails["source"]`

## Using it

- Each part is a standalone directive on the caller's own element: `<button kuiDialogTrigger>`. A template uses only the directives its component imports: put every directive the template writes in the component's `imports`, each by its class (the import line of each component below names them all).
- The package has one entry for the components: every directive is imported from `@kirana-ui/angular`.
- Props are inputs. Bind them (`[defaultValue]="'a'"`): a static attribute stays on the element. An `id` is given as `[kuiId]`.
- A value binds two ways with `[(value)]` (`[(open)]`, `[(page)]` …); the output with the details is `(valueChanged)="…($event.value, $event.details)"` (`(openChanged)`, `(pageChanged)` …). Below, `[(name)]` is such a model and `(name)` an output.
- A part that draws a list is structural and gives each entry: `*kuiDateFieldSegments="let segment"`.
- A structural directive's own value is written after its name, and its other inputs after a semicolon: `*kuiTabsPanel="'account'; keepMounted: true"`.
- A select's value written structurally draws its own content with what is chosen: `<span *kuiSelectValue="let shown">{{ shown.label }}</span>` (`shown.value`, `shown.label`; with `multiple`, `shown.values` and `shown.labels`, in the items' order).
- A positioner's `[anchor]` is an element (a template variable, `#box`), an `ElementRef`, an object with `getBoundingClientRect`, or a function that gives one of those (a `viewChild` signal).
- Angular 20 and later, with signals; it renders on a server and hydrates.
- What the other frameworks call `PortalProvider` and `DirectionProvider` are the directives `kuiPortalProvider` (`[container]`) and `kuiDirection` here, and `useDirection` is `injectDirection()`.
- Each component's "Anatomy" is where its parts go: a part is written inside the part it is indented under, with elements of your own between them where the design needs any. `(optional)` marks a wrapper that may be left out, what it holds then written where the wrapper would be; `(repeated)` a part written once for each entry (an item, a tab, a toast), or any number of times; `(as above)` a part drawn in full where it first appears. It is the library's own data (`inside`, `optional` and `repeated` on each part of `@kirana-ui/vocabulary`), held against the pages the library is tested with: write a part nowhere else.
- A part that is in the page only some of the time, or that is drawn once for each entry of a list, is a structural directive, written with `*` on the element it draws: `*kuiAccordionPanel`, `*kuiDialogPortal`, `*kuiComboboxClear`, `*kuiComboboxPortal`, `*kuiComboboxCollection`, `*kuiComboboxEmpty`, `*kuiAvatarImage`, `*kuiAvatarFallback`, `*kuiCalendarMonths`, `*kuiCalendarWeekdays`, `*kuiCalendarWeeks`, `*kuiCheckboxIndicator`, `*kuiCollapsiblePanel`, `*kuiComboboxValue`, `*kuiComboboxItemIndicator`, `*kuiCommandEmpty`, `*kuiMenuPortal`, `*kuiMenuCheckboxItemIndicator`, `*kuiMenuRadioItemIndicator`, `*kuiDateFieldSegments`, `*kuiPopoverPortal`, `*kuiFieldError`, `*kuiFieldValidity`, `*kuiHoverCardPortal`, `*kuiListboxItemIndicator`, `*kuiNavigationMenuContent`, `*kuiNavigationMenuPortal`, `*kuiNumberFieldScrubAreaCursor`, `*kuiOtpCaret`, `*kuiPaginationItems`, `*kuiRadioGroupIndicator`, `*kuiScrollAreaScrollbar`, `*kuiScrollAreaCorner`, `*kuiSelectValue`, `*kuiSelectPortal`, `*kuiSelectScrollUpArrow`, `*kuiSelectScrollDownArrow`, `*kuiSelectItemIndicator`, `*kuiTabsPanel`, `*kuiToastList` and `*kuiTooltipPortal`. No other directive is written with `*`: a popup, a positioner and a backdrop are plain directives inside their structural portal (`<ng-container *kuiDialogPortal><div kuiDialogBackdrop></div><div kuiDialogPopup>…</div></ng-container>`).
- A root that draws nothing can sit on `<ng-container>`. A directive with an `exportAs` is reached from the template: `#tabs="kuiTabs"`.
- A popup is drawn in a portal at the end of `<body>`. In `Autocomplete`, `Combobox`, `ContextMenu`, `DatePicker`, `HoverCard`, `Menu`, `NavigationMenu`, `Popover`, `Select` and `Tooltip` it is `Portal` > `Positioner` > `Popup`: the `Positioner` places it against its trigger and carries `--anchor-width`, `--available-height`, `--transform-origin` and `data-side`. `AlertDialog`, `Dialog` and `Drawer` have no `Positioner`: there it is `Portal` > `Backdrop` and `Popup`, and the design places the popup. A dialog and an alert dialog may put the `Popup` in a `Viewport`, the box a long one scrolls in.
- Every `Positioner` takes the same options (`side`, `align`, `sideOffset`, `alignOffset`, `collisionPadding`, `collisionBoundary`, `collisionAvoidance`, `sticky`, `arrowPadding`, `positionMethod`, `anchor`), listed once under "Positioner options" with their defaults. An anchor may change while the popup is open, and the popup follows.
- Every change callback is an output whose event is `{ value, details }` under the value's own name (`$event.open`, `$event.values`): `details.reason`, `details.event`, `details.source` (mouse, touch, pen, keyboard, virtual, programmatic, agent), and `details.cancel()` to keep the value as it was. An output that reports something that happened carries only that, and cannot be refused: `(clearErrors)`, `(completed)` and `(loadingStatusChanged)`.
- A part that is in the page only while it is open, chosen or checked leaves it otherwise. `keepMounted` keeps it in the page, hidden, on the parts that take it and no others: `[kuiAccordionPanel]`, `[kuiCollapsiblePanel]`, `[kuiScrollAreaScrollbar]` and `[kuiTabsPanel]`.
- `readOnly` (shown, focusable, not changeable) is a prop of `Autocomplete`, `Calendar`, `Checkbox`, `Combobox`, `DateField`, `DatePicker`, `NumberField`, `RadioGroup`, `Select`, `Slider` and `Switch` and of no other component.
- No CSS is shipped and no styles are injected. A part is styled by its element, its `class`, and the attributes and CSS variables listed for it below.
- A boolean state is an attribute that is present or absent (`[data-open]`), never `="false"`.
- An entrance starts from `[data-starting-style]` and an exit ends at `[data-ending-style]`: write the hidden style under both and transition between. A part leaves the page when its own motion has ended.
- A value is controlled when it is given (`value`) and the component's own when it is not (`defaultValue`). `open`/`defaultOpen` and the others pair the same way.
- A control with a `name` is submitted with the form around it and follows the form's reset. Inside a `Field` it is the field's control.
- `PortalProvider` (`container`) says where the popups inside it are drawn, in place of the end of `<body>`: a shadow root's host, a full-screen element.
- An agent can read and use a page built with these: `createAgent()` from `@kirana-ui/angular/agent` gives `snapshot()`, `act({ steps })`, `query()`, `history()`, `undo()` and `redo()`; what it changes reaches the same callbacks with `details.source === "agent"`. "Agent", above, has the whole of it.

### For a design system

- A design system's part is a directive of its own that hosts the primitive's: `@Directive({ selector: "[uiDialog]", hostDirectives: [{ directive: KuiDialog, inputs: ["kuiId", "open", "defaultOpen"], outputs: ["openChange", "openChanged"] }] })`. Angular binds a host directive's inputs and outputs only where the host exposes them (`inputs`, `outputs`, each `"name"` or `"name: alias"`): expose what its callers set, and give the rest yourself (below). Its own host bindings (`host: { class: "…", "[attr.data-size]": "size()" }`) join the element's: classes are joined, and both handlers of an event run. An element of the design system's own (a badge) is such a directive with no primitive: nothing of the library's is needed for it.
- Keep the design system's selectors apart from the primitives' `kui…`: two directives with one selector in one template's `imports` both match the element, silently (Angular says nothing), and a part would then be made twice. Name your own `[ui…]`, `[my…]`, anything but `kui`.
- A model's output, `openChange` beside `[(open)]` (`valueChange`, `pageChange` …), carries the model's type, `boolean | undefined` for `open`: its first value can be the `undefined` the model starts with. Expose it with the model's input for a two-way `[(open)]` on the design system's directive, or expose `openChanged` for the change with its details.
- A part that comes and goes is structural (`*kuiDialogPortal`), and an attribute cannot put a structural directive around its own element: draw it in a component's template around `<ng-content />`. `@Component({ selector: "[uiDialogContent]", imports: [KuiDialogPortal, KuiDialogBackdrop, KuiDialogPopup], template: `<ng-template kuiDialogPortal><div kuiDialogBackdrop></div><div kuiDialogPopup><ng-content /></div></ng-template>` })`. A part given to it (`<h2 uiDialogTitle>`) is made where it is written, so it finds its root there, inside the design system's `[uiDialog]`, not where it is drawn: the title labels the popup.
- `hostInputs(directive, given)` gives a primitive the design system hosts its inputs, where its callers do not: call it in the hosting directive's constructor or a field initialiser, with each value a function read like a signal, so one worked out from the design system's own inputs follows them: `hostInputs(KuiTooltip, { delay: () => 0, disabled: computed(() => !this.collapsed()) })`, `hostInputs(KuiCommand, { filter: computed(() => (this.shouldFilter() ? undefined : null)) })`, `hostInputs(KuiTooltipPositioner, { sideOffset: () => 4 })`. An input the element binds, one the host exposes and its caller writes, wins over what is given. It is typed against the primitive's inputs (`HostInputs<KuiTooltip>`, `InputsOf<KuiTooltip>`), and an input that does not reach the component (a structural directive's own value) throws when the primitive starts. No subclass of a primitive is needed for any of this.
- Tooltips need no provider: one is open at a time across the page, and while one shows the next opens without its wait, by themselves. A tooltip waits 600 ms before it opens (a hover card 600 ms, and 300 ms before it closes). A design system whose tooltips open at once gives `delay` to the tooltip it hosts: `hostInputs(KuiTooltip, { delay: () => 0 })`, exposing `delay` so a caller can still set it.

## Components

### Accordion

```
import { KuiAccordion, KuiAccordionItem, KuiAccordionHeader, KuiAccordionTrigger, KuiAccordionPanel } from "@kirana-ui/angular"
```

Parts: `[kuiAccordion]`, `[kuiAccordionItem]`, `[kuiAccordionHeader]`, `[kuiAccordionTrigger]`, `[kuiAccordionPanel]`.

Anatomy:

```
kuiAccordion
  kuiAccordionItem (repeated)
    kuiAccordionHeader
      kuiAccordionTrigger
    *kuiAccordionPanel
```

Props of its root:

- `[(value)]: readonly Value[]`: The values of the open items.
- `defaultValue?: readonly Value[]`: Read once.
- `multiple?: boolean`: Whether several items can be open at once. Default `false`: opening one closes the others.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disables every item: none can be opened or closed.
- `orientation?: Orientation`: The way the arrows move between triggers. Default `vertical`.
- `loop?: boolean`: Whether the arrows wrap from the last trigger to the first. Default `true`.
- `(valueChanged): { value: Value[]; details: ChangeDetails }`: The change with why it happened; `details.cancel()` keeps the value.

Each part, and its own props:

- `[kuiAccordion]` is `KuiAccordion`. `exportAs: "kuiAccordion"`. Generic: `<Value = unknown>`. Its props are above.
- `[kuiAccordionItem]` is `KuiAccordionItem`. `value` tells this item from the others; an item that is given none makes its own.
    - `value?: unknown`: What tells this item from the others: it is in the accordion's `value` while the item is open. An item that is given none makes its own.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables this item: it cannot be opened or closed.
- `[kuiAccordionHeader]` is `KuiAccordionHeader`.
- `[kuiAccordionTrigger]` is `KuiAccordionTrigger`.
- `[kuiAccordionPanel]` is `KuiAccordionPanel`. Structural: written `*kuiAccordionPanel`. `<div *kuiAccordionPanel>`: in the page while open; `{ keepMounted: true }` keeps it, hidden.
    - `*kuiAccordionPanel: { keepMounted?: boolean } | ""`: The directive's own value: `*kuiAccordionPanel="…"`. Its options: `{ keepMounted: true }` keeps the panel in the page, hidden, while its item is closed.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: Groups the items.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the items are laid out, and the arrows that move between their triggers.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- item: One section: a header with its trigger, and a panel. Its `value` tells it from the others; an item that is given none makes its own.
    - `data-open`: Present when the item is open.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- header: The heading that holds the trigger.
    - `data-open`: Present when the item is open.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- trigger: The button that opens and closes the item's panel.
    - `data-panel-open`: Present when the item's panel is open.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- panel: The item's content. In the page while open, and through its exit's motion.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the items are laid out, and the arrows that move between their triggers.
    - `--accordion-panel-height`: The panel's content height while it opens or closes, `auto` once it is open.
    - `--accordion-panel-width`: The panel's content width while it opens or closes, `auto` once it is open.

### AlertDialog

```
import { KuiAlertDialog, KuiDialogTrigger, KuiDialogPortal, KuiDialogBackdrop, KuiDialogViewport, KuiDialogPopup, KuiDialogTitle, KuiDialogDescription, KuiDialogClose } from "@kirana-ui/angular"
```

Parts: `[kuiAlertDialog]`, `[kuiDialogTrigger]`, `[kuiDialogPortal]`, `[kuiDialogBackdrop]`, `[kuiDialogViewport]`, `[kuiDialogPopup]`, `[kuiDialogTitle]`, `[kuiDialogDescription]`, `[kuiDialogClose]`.

Anatomy:

```
kuiAlertDialog
  kuiDialogTrigger
  *kuiDialogPortal
    kuiDialogBackdrop
    kuiDialogViewport (optional)
      kuiDialogPopup
        kuiDialogTitle
        kuiDialogDescription
        kuiDialogClose
```

Props of its root:

- `[(open)]: boolean`: Whether it is open, when the caller holds it.
- `defaultOpen?: boolean`: Whether it starts open, when the caller does not hold `open`. Read once.
- `(openChanged): { open: boolean; details: ChangeDetails }`: Heard as it is about to open or close: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.

Each part, and its own props:

- `[kuiAlertDialog]` is `KuiAlertDialog`. `exportAs: "kuiDialog"`. `kuiAlertDialog`, on any element or on `<ng-container>`: a dialog that asks for an answer. It is always modal and a press outside it never closes it, so it takes neither `[modal]` nor `[dismissible]`. Its parts are a dialog's (`kuiDialogTrigger`, `kuiDialogPopup` …), which find it as their root. Its props are above.
- `[kuiDialogTrigger]` is `KuiDialogTrigger`.
- `[kuiDialogPortal]` is `KuiDialogPortal`. Structural: written `*kuiDialogPortal`. `<ng-template kuiDialogPortal>` or `*kuiDialogPortal`: its content at the end of the page while open.
- `[kuiDialogBackdrop]` is `KuiDialogBackdrop`.
- `[kuiDialogViewport]` is `KuiDialogViewport`. What a long dialog scrolls in, around its popup: it may be left out. A dialog's and an alert dialog's; a drawer lies at an edge of the page and has none.
- `[kuiDialogPopup]` is `KuiDialogPopup`.
- `[kuiDialogTitle]` is `KuiDialogTitle`. The heading that names the dialog.
- `[kuiDialogDescription]` is `KuiDialogDescription`. The text that describes the dialog.
- `[kuiDialogClose]` is `KuiDialogClose`. A button that closes the dialog.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- trigger: The button that opens the dialog.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when the dialog is open.
- backdrop: The layer over the page behind the dialog.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
- viewport: What a long dialog scrolls in: it lies over the page, between the backdrop and the popup. A press on it beside the popup is a press outside the dialog; a press on its scrollbar is not.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-nested`: Present when the dialog opened over another dialog.
    - `data-nested-dialog-open`: Present when another dialog is open above this one.
- popup: The dialog itself.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-nested-dialog-open`: Present when another dialog is open above this one.
    - `--nested-dialogs`: How many dialogs are open above this one.

### Autocomplete

```
import { KuiCombobox, KuiComboboxInput, KuiComboboxTrigger, KuiComboboxClear, KuiComboboxPortal, KuiComboboxPositioner, KuiComboboxPopup, KuiComboboxList, KuiComboboxCollection, KuiComboboxGroup, KuiComboboxGroupLabel, KuiComboboxSeparator, KuiComboboxItem, KuiComboboxEmpty, KuiComboboxStatus } from "@kirana-ui/angular"
```

Parts: `[kuiAutocomplete]`, `input[kuiComboboxInput]`, `[kuiComboboxTrigger]`, `[kuiComboboxClear]`, `[kuiComboboxPortal]`, `[kuiComboboxPositioner]`, `[kuiComboboxPopup]`, `[kuiComboboxList]`, `[kuiComboboxCollection]`, `[kuiComboboxGroup]`, `[kuiComboboxGroupLabel]`, `[kuiComboboxSeparator]`, `[kuiComboboxItem]`, `[kuiComboboxEmpty]`, `[kuiComboboxStatus]`.

Anatomy:

```
kuiAutocomplete
  input[kuiComboboxInput]
  kuiComboboxTrigger
  *kuiComboboxPortal
    kuiComboboxPositioner
      kuiComboboxPopup
        kuiComboboxList (optional)
          *kuiComboboxCollection (optional)
            kuiComboboxItem (repeated, as above)
            kuiComboboxGroup (optional, repeated, as above)
          kuiComboboxGroup (optional, repeated)
            *kuiComboboxCollection (optional, as above)
            kuiComboboxItem (repeated)
            kuiComboboxGroupLabel
          kuiComboboxSeparator (repeated)
        *kuiComboboxCollection (optional, as above)
        *kuiComboboxEmpty
        kuiComboboxStatus (optional)
  kuiComboboxPopup (as above)
  kuiComboboxStatus (optional, as above)
  *kuiComboboxClear
```

Props of its root:

- `[(value)]: Value | null`: What the input says: the text is the value.
- `defaultValue?: NoInfer<Value> | null`: The text it starts with, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
- `[(inputValue)]: string`: What the input says, `[(inputValue)]`. With `kuiAutocomplete` the text is `[(value)]`.
- `defaultInputValue?: string`: The text the input starts with, when the caller does not hold `inputValue`. Read once.
- `[(open)]: boolean`: Whether the list is open, when the caller holds it.
- `defaultOpen?: boolean`: Whether the list starts open, when the caller does not hold `open`. Read once.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: it cannot be changed.
- `readOnly?: boolean`: Its value can be read and not changed: the list still opens and can be gone through, but no press and no Enter chooses, nothing typed is taken, and its clear and chip buttons do nothing. Its value is still submitted.
- `name?: string`: The input's name in the form around it.
- `form?: string`: The id of the form the control belongs to, when it is not inside it.
- `items?: readonly ComboboxItemData<Value>[] | readonly ComboboxGroupData<Value>[] | Readonly<Record<string, string>>`: The values with their labels: a list of them, groups of them (`{ value, items }`), or the labels by value. With a `*kuiComboboxCollection` it is the list itself: the combobox filters it, and the collection draws what is left.
- `filter?: ((label: string, query: string) => boolean) | null`: Whether an item is shown for what was typed; `null` shows every item.
- `required?: boolean`: In a field, "none" is then wrong.
- `multiple?: boolean`: Several values, each shown as a chip: they are `values`, not `value`.
- `[(values)]: readonly Value[]`: With `multiple`: the chosen values, in the order they were chosen, `[(values)]`.
- `defaultValues?: readonly Value[]`: With `multiple`: the values it starts with, when the caller does not hold `values`. Read once.
- `(valuesChanged): { values: Value[]; details: ChangeDetails }`: With `multiple`: heard as a value is about to be added or taken away; `details.cancel()` keeps the values as they were.
- `inline?: boolean`: The list is always in the page, with no popup: a command palette.
- `virtualized?: ListCollection`: Every row, when only some are in the page: each item is then given its `index`.
- `autoHighlight?: boolean`: The first item shown for what was typed is highlighted as one types, so Enter chooses it. Off by default.
- `mode?: "list" | "none"`: With `kuiAutocomplete`: `"none"` shows the suggestions as the caller draws them.
- `openOnInputClick?: boolean`: With `kuiAutocomplete`: a press on the input opens the list.
- `(valueChanged): { value: Value | null; details: ChangeDetails }`: Heard as the text is about to change, typed or chosen: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.
- `(inputValueChanged): { value: string; details: ChangeDetails }`: Heard as the input's text is about to change; `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.
- `(openChanged): { open: boolean; details: ChangeDetails }`: Heard as the list is about to open or close: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.

Each part, and its own props:

- `[kuiAutocomplete]` is `KuiCombobox`. `exportAs: "kuiCombobox"`. Generic: `<Value = unknown>`. `kuiAutocomplete` is a combobox whose text is the value: `[(value)]` is the text, and the list only suggests. Its parts are the combobox's directives. Its props are above.
- `input[kuiComboboxInput]` is `KuiComboboxInput`. `<input kuiComboboxInput>`: what is typed filters the list, which is placed against it.
- `[kuiComboboxTrigger]` is `KuiComboboxTrigger`.
- `[kuiComboboxClear]` is `KuiComboboxClear`. Structural: written `*kuiComboboxClear`. `<button *kuiComboboxClear>`: empties the input and the value; in the page while there is something to clear.
- `[kuiComboboxPortal]` is `KuiComboboxPortal`. Structural: written `*kuiComboboxPortal`. Draws what it holds at the end of `<body>`, or in the container a `PortalProvider` names.
- `[kuiComboboxPositioner]` is `KuiComboboxPositioner`. Takes the positioner options ("Positioner options", above).
- `[kuiComboboxPopup]` is `KuiComboboxPopup`.
- `[kuiComboboxList]` is `KuiComboboxList`. The items' own box inside the popup, when the popup holds more than items (an input): it is then the listbox.
- `[kuiComboboxCollection]` is `KuiComboboxCollection`. Structural: written `*kuiComboboxCollection`. Its template is given the entry: `let entry` is a `ComboboxEntry`. `<ng-container *kuiComboboxCollection="let entry">` draws the list from the root's `items`: once for each item left for what was typed, or for each group that has items left. With `of` (`*kuiComboboxCollection="let item; of: group"`), for each of that group's items left. The root then filters, and no item hides itself.
    - `of?: ComboboxEntry`: Written after the directive's value: `*kuiComboboxCollection="…; of: …"`. A group the root's `items` gave: its items left are then what is drawn.
- `[kuiComboboxGroup]` is `KuiComboboxGroup`. Items that belong together, named by their `kuiComboboxGroupLabel`. Hidden while none is shown.
- `[kuiComboboxGroupLabel]` is `KuiComboboxGroupLabel`. Names the group it is in. With no group around it, it is plain text.
- `[kuiComboboxSeparator]` is `KuiComboboxSeparator`. A line between groups.
- `[kuiComboboxItem]` is `KuiComboboxItem`.
    - `value: unknown`: Required. What the combobox's value is while this item is chosen.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables this item: it cannot be chosen, and the arrows pass over it.
    - `label?: string`: What is filtered and what the input shows; the item's text when left out.
    - `index?: number`: Its place among all the rows, in a virtualized list.
- `[kuiComboboxEmpty]` is `KuiComboboxEmpty`. Structural: written `*kuiComboboxEmpty`. `<div *kuiComboboxEmpty>`: in the page while no item is shown for what was typed.
- `[kuiComboboxStatus]` is `KuiComboboxStatus`. Says how the list stands ("3 results", "Loading") to software that reads the page, as its text changes. Keep it in the page and change what it holds: inside the popup, or beside the input.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- input: The text input: its text is the value, and what is typed asks for suggestions.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when the list is open.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
- trigger: A button that opens and closes the list. With the input inside the popup it is the combobox: a stop for Tab, and what the popup is placed against.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when the list is open.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
- positioner: Places the list against the input: against the chips' box when the input is in one, the button when the input is inside the popup, or its own `anchor`. It carries the geometry.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `--anchor-width`: The anchor's width.
    - `--anchor-height`: The anchor's height.
    - `--available-width`: The width between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--available-height`: The height between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--transform-origin`: The point of the popup nearest its anchor, to scale from.
- popup: The list of items. With a `list` inside, what holds it: a dialog around an input and the list.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-empty`: Present when no item is shown for what was typed.
- list: The items' own box inside the popup, when the popup holds more than items (an input): it is then the listbox.
    - `data-empty`: Present when no item is shown for what was typed.
- item: One suggestion: chosen, its text is written into the input.
    - `data-selected`: Present on the chosen item.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the pointer or the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- clear: A button that empties the input and the value.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

### Autosize

```
import { KuiAutosizeTextarea } from "@kirana-ui/angular"
```

Parts: `textarea[kuiAutosizeTextarea]`.

Anatomy:

```
textarea[kuiAutosizeTextarea]
```

Each part, and its own props:

- `textarea[kuiAutosizeTextarea]` is `KuiAutosizeTextarea`. `exportAs: "kuiAutosizeTextarea"`. `<textarea kuiAutosizeTextarea>`: as tall as its text.

### Avatar

```
import { KuiAvatar, KuiAvatarImage, KuiAvatarFallback } from "@kirana-ui/angular"
```

Parts: `[kuiAvatar]`, `[kuiAvatarImage]`, `[kuiAvatarFallback]`.

Anatomy:

```
kuiAvatar
  *kuiAvatarImage
  *kuiAvatarFallback
```

Props of its root:

- `(loadingStatusChanged): ImageStatus`: Each time the picture's loading status changes: `loading` once it has an address, then `loaded` or `error`; `idle` again when its address is taken away. Base UI's `onLoadingStatusChange`; the root says the same in `data-image-loading-status`.

Each part, and its own props:

- `[kuiAvatar]` is `KuiAvatar`. `exportAs: "kuiAvatar"`. `<span kuiAvatar>`: the frame. `(loadingStatusChanged)` hears its picture's loading, in either of the image's forms (a structural directive's own outputs cannot be bound from its element). Its props are above.
- `[kuiAvatarImage]` is `KuiAvatarImage`. Structural: written `*kuiAvatarImage`. The picture, in either of two forms. `<img *kuiAvatarImage="address" alt="…">` is in the page once the picture has loaded. `<img kuiAvatarImage [src]="address" alt="…">` is the caller's own element, kept in the page as Base UI's `keepMounted` image: it loads the picture itself (`loading="lazy"` works), its own `src` is the address and is followed as it changes, and until it has loaded it is `aria-hidden`, with `data-loading` or `data-error` for the design to hide or fade it by. The root's `(loadingStatusChanged)` hears the loading either way.
    - `*kuiAvatarImage: string`: The directive's own value: `*kuiAvatarImage="…"`. The picture's address, in the structural form: the element is in the page once it has loaded.
- `[kuiAvatarFallback]` is `KuiAvatarFallback`. Structural: written `*kuiAvatarFallback`. `<span *kuiAvatarFallback>`: what shows until the picture has loaded, or when it cannot. `{ delay: 600 }` waits that many milliseconds first, so a picture that loads sooner never lets it be seen.
    - `*kuiAvatarFallback: { delay?: number | undefined } | ""`: The directive's own value: `*kuiAvatarFallback="…"`. Its options: `{ delay: 600 }` waits that many milliseconds before showing. Read once. Default: no wait.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The frame the image and its stand-in share.
    - `data-image-loading-status="idle | loading | loaded | error"`: Where the picture is in its loading: `idle` while it has no address.
- image: The picture. In the page once it has loaded; with `keepMounted` (on Angular, the attribute form) in the page all along, `aria-hidden` until it has loaded.
    - `data-loading`: Present while the picture loads, on an image kept in the page.
    - `data-error`: Present when the picture cannot load, on an image kept in the page.

### Button

```
import { KuiButton } from "@kirana-ui/angular"
```

Props:

- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: a press does nothing.
- `focusableWhenDisabled?: boolean`: Keeps a disabled button in the tab order, so what it would do can still be read.
- `nativeButton?: boolean`: `false` when the element is not a `<button>`: it is given a button's role and keyboard. Default `true`.

`[kuiButton]` is `KuiButton`. `exportAs: "kuiButton"`. On a `<button>`, or with `[nativeButton]="false"` on another element that acts as one.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The button.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

### Calendar

```
import { KuiCalendar, KuiCalendarHeading, KuiCalendarPrevious, KuiCalendarNext, KuiCalendarMonths, KuiCalendarGrid, KuiCalendarWeekdays, KuiCalendarHeadCell, KuiCalendarWeeks, KuiCalendarCell, KuiCalendarDay, KuiCalendarInput } from "@kirana-ui/angular"
```

Parts: `[kuiCalendar]`, `[kuiCalendarHeading]`, `[kuiCalendarPrevious]`, `[kuiCalendarNext]`, `[kuiCalendarMonths]`, `[kuiCalendarGrid]`, `[kuiCalendarWeekdays]`, `[kuiCalendarHeadCell]`, `[kuiCalendarWeeks]`, `[kuiCalendarCell]`, `[kuiCalendarDay]`, `input[kuiCalendarInput]`.

Anatomy:

```
kuiCalendar
  *kuiCalendarMonths (optional)
    kuiCalendarHeading
    kuiCalendarGrid
      *kuiCalendarWeekdays
        kuiCalendarHeadCell (repeated)
      *kuiCalendarWeeks
        kuiCalendarCell (repeated)
          kuiCalendarDay
  kuiCalendarPrevious
  kuiCalendarNext
  input[kuiCalendarInput]
```

Props of its root:

- `[(value)]: CalendarValueOf<Mode>`: One day; with `mode="range"` a first and a last; with `mode="multiple"` a list: `[(value)]`. Typed by `mode`.
- `defaultValue?: NoInfer<CalendarValueOf<Mode>>`: The value it starts with, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
- `mode?: Mode`: One day (the default), a first and a last (`"range"`), or any number (`"multiple"`).
- `minDays?: number`: With `mode="multiple"`: the fewest days that can be left chosen.
- `maxDays?: number`: With `mode="multiple"`: the most days that can be chosen.
- `months?: number`: How many months are shown side by side, each drawn by `*kuiCalendarMonths`. Default `1`.
- `pagedNavigation?: boolean`: With several `months`: Previous and Next turn them all rather than one month.
- `[(month)]: string`: The first day of the month shown (any day of it): `[(month)]`.
- `defaultMonth?: string`: The month it starts on, when the caller does not hold `month`. Read once.
- `defaultFocusedValue?: string`: The day it opens on, focusable when Tab reaches the grid. It is also the month it opens on, unless `month` or `defaultMonth` says another: then the stop for Tab is a chosen day of the months shown, today, or their first day.
- `locale?: string`: The language and region its names, first day of the week and calendar follow. Default `"en-US"`.
- `calendarSystem?: CalendarSystem`: The calendar its months are laid out in, when it is not the Gregorian one.
- `min?: string`: The first and the last day that can be chosen.
- `max?: string`: The last day that can be chosen.
- `isDateUnavailable?: (date: string) => boolean`: Days that cannot be chosen, though they can be reached: a day off, a day taken.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: no day can be chosen.
- `readOnly?: boolean`: Shown as it is: the days can be moved through, and none can be chosen.
- `fixedWeeks?: boolean`: Always six rows, so the calendar is one height in every month.
- `name?: string`: The name its hidden input (`kuiCalendarInput`) submits the value under.
